Harmonized Drug Dataset Quality Control

James Bannon, Michael Tran

March 31, 2026

1 Overview

This report is a quality control walkthrough for the Harmonized Drug Dataset stored as a MultiAssayExperiment (MAE). The dataset harmonizes multiple drug-related assays and features across a shared compound universe (PubChem CID) so downstream analyses can operate on a consistent sample space.

1.1 Data Sources

The MAE is constructed in workflow/scripts/construct_MAE.R. It pulls processed experiments from data/procdata/experiments/ and a colData table from data/procdata/colData.csv. Key sources (from config/pipeline.yaml and the workflow scripts) include:

  • BindingDB: compound-by-target affinity measurements sourced from BindingDB.
  • DeepChem datasets (Tox21, ToxCast, SIDER, ClinTox): downloaded from DeepChem S3, then re-shaped to CID-by-assay matrices.
  • JUMP-CP We accessed the compound info from the JUMP-CP dataset created by the Broad Institute.
  • LINCS We accessed the compound info from the 2020 release of the LINCS L1000 perturbatione experiments. These experiments were also conducted by the Broad Institute.
  • Bioassays: pulled from the BHKLab AnnotationDB alongside compound metadata, then filtered to gold-standard assays.
  • Fingerprints: RDKit Morgan count fingerprints generated from SMILES.

2 Load HDD

library(MultiAssayExperiment)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(Matrix)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(glmnet)

hdd_mae <- readRDS("data/results/HDD_v1.1.RDS")
hdd_mae
## A MultiAssayExperiment object of 10 listed
##  experiments with user-defined names and respective classes.
##  Containing an ExperimentList class object of length 10:
##  [1] SIDER: SummarizedExperiment with 27 rows and 1410 columns
##  [2] Bioassays: SummarizedExperiment with 33 rows and 422030 columns
##  [3] Tox21: SummarizedExperiment with 12 rows and 5396 columns
##  [4] ToxCast: SummarizedExperiment with 617 rows and 6054 columns
##  [5] ClinTox: SummarizedExperiment with 2 rows and 885 columns
##  [6] fingerprint.Morgan.2.1024: SummarizedExperiment with 1024 rows and 422030 columns
##  [7] fingerprint.Morgan.2.2048: SummarizedExperiment with 2048 rows and 422030 columns
##  [8] fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024: SummarizedExperiment with 1024 rows and 422030 columns
##  [9] fingerprint.Morgan.3.2048: SummarizedExperiment with 2048 rows and 422030 columns
##  [10] BindingDB: SummarizedExperiment with 837 rows and 1183 columns
## Functionality:
##  experiments() - obtain the ExperimentList instance
##  colData() - the primary/phenotype DataFrame
##  sampleMap() - the sample coordination DataFrame
##  `$`, `[`, `[[` - extract colData columns, subset, or experiment
##  *Format() - convert into a long or wide DataFrame
##  assays() - convert ExperimentList to a SimpleList of matrices
##  exportClass() - save data to flat files
compound_labels <- as.data.frame(colData(hdd_mae)) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("sample_id") |>
  transmute(
    sample_id = as.character(sample_id),
    compound_label = dplyr::coalesce(
      na_if(trimws(as.character(Molecule.Name)), ""),
      na_if(trimws(as.character(IUPAC.Name)), ""),
      na_if(trimws(as.character(Pubchem.CID)), ""),
      sample_id
    )
  )

compound_labels$compound_label <- make.unique(compound_labels$compound_label)

3 MAE snapshot

experiment_names <- names(experiments(hdd_mae))
experiment_names
##  [1] "SIDER"                     "Bioassays"                
##  [3] "Tox21"                     "ToxCast"                  
##  [5] "ClinTox"                   "fingerprint.Morgan.2.1024"
##  [7] "fingerprint.Morgan.2.2048" "fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024"
##  [9] "fingerprint.Morgan.3.2048" "BindingDB"
has_experiment <- function(name) {
  name %in% experiment_names
}

summarize_experiment <- function(se) {
  assay_obj <- assays(se)[[1]]
  data_class <- class(assay_obj)[1]
  dims <- dim(assay_obj)
  missing_fraction <- if (is.numeric(assay_obj) || is.logical(assay_obj)) {
    mean(is.na(assay_obj))
  } else {
    mean(is.na(as.vector(assay_obj)))
  }

  data.frame(
    assay_name = assayNames(se)[1],
    rows = dims[1],
    cols = dims[2],
    data_class = data_class,
    missing_fraction = missing_fraction,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

experiment_summary <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(experiments(hdd_mae), summarize_experiment)
)
rownames(experiment_summary) <- experiment_names
experiment_summary

Basic sanity checks for sampleMap completeness.

# Basic sampleMap sanity checks
all_in_coldata <- lapply(experiments(hdd_mae), function(se) {
  all(colnames(se) %in% rownames(colData(hdd_mae)))
})
if (all(unlist(all_in_coldata))) {
  print("All experiments map cleanly to colData.")
} else {
  print("Some experiments contain samples missing from colData:")
  print(all_in_coldata[!unlist(all_in_coldata)])
}
## [1] "All experiments map cleanly to colData."
# Any missing samples per experiment (only report issues)
missing_samples <- lapply(experiments(hdd_mae), function(se) {
  setdiff(colnames(se), rownames(colData(hdd_mae)))
})
missing_samples <- missing_samples[lengths(missing_samples) > 0]
if (length(missing_samples) == 0) {
  print("No missing samples detected in any experiment.")
} else {
  print("Missing samples by experiment:")
  print(missing_samples)
}
## [1] "No missing samples detected in any experiment."

5 Experiment walkthroughs

Below, each experiment in the HDD MAE is reviewed.

5.1 BindingDB

BindingDB contributes a compound-by-target affinity matrix derived from curated binding measurements.

se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[["BindingDB"]]
assay_mat <- assay(se)

# Dimensions and a small preview
c(rows = nrow(assay_mat), cols = ncol(assay_mat))
## rows cols 
##  837 1183
assay_mat[1:min(5, nrow(assay_mat)), 1:min(6, ncol(assay_mat))]
##                                        681 8223 3559  3696 4543 5775
## Beta-2 adrenergic receptor           61000   NA 5000    NA   NA   NA
## 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 1B         NA  2.1  270    NA   NA   NA
## Leukotriene B4 receptor 2               NA   NA   NA    NA   NA   NA
## Muscarinic acetylcholine receptor M1    NA   NA   NA 42.00   40   NA
## Muscarinic acetylcholine receptor M2    NA   NA   NA  0.13  110   NA
# Missingness by target and compound
row_missing <- rowMeans(is.na(assay_mat))
col_missing <- colMeans(is.na(assay_mat))
summary(row_missing)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   0.913   0.988   0.996   0.992   0.999   0.999
summary(col_missing)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   0.712   0.995   0.998   0.992   0.999   0.999
# Value distribution (numeric only)
summary(as.numeric(assay_mat))
##     Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max.     NA's 
## 0.00e+00 6.00e+01 6.30e+02 1.33e+05 2.80e+03 5.00e+08   981890
bindingdb_missing <- tibble::tibble(
  missing_fraction = c(row_missing, col_missing),
  axis = rep(c("Target", "Compound"), c(length(row_missing), length(col_missing)))
)

ggplot(bindingdb_missing, aes(x = missing_fraction, fill = axis)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "BindingDB missingness by target vs compound",
    x = "Missing fraction",
    y = "Count",
    fill = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

bindingdb_vals <- as.numeric(assay_mat)
bindingdb_vals <- bindingdb_vals[!is.na(bindingdb_vals) & bindingdb_vals > 0]

ggplot(tibble::tibble(log10_affinity = log10(bindingdb_vals)), aes(x = log10_affinity)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#3A6EA5", alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "BindingDB affinity values (log10 nM)",
    x = "log10(affinity nM)",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

5.2 Bioassays

A compound-by-assay matrix of PubChem bioassay outcomes. Rows are AIDs (assay identifiers) and columns are PubChem CIDs. Entries are categorical outcomes, with missing values representing compounds that were not measured.

se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[["Bioassays"]]
assay_mat <- assay(se)

c(rows = nrow(assay_mat), cols = ncol(assay_mat))
##   rows   cols 
##     33 422030
assay_mat[1:min(5, nrow(assay_mat)), 1:min(6, ncol(assay_mat))]
# Category counts
assay_mat_chr <- as.matrix(assay_mat)
assay_values <- ifelse(is.na(assay_mat_chr), "Not Measured", as.character(assay_mat_chr))
category_counts <- sort(table(assay_values), decreasing = TRUE)
category_counts
## assay_values
## Not Measured       Active 
##     13352761       574229
inactive_count <- if ("Inactive" %in% names(category_counts)) category_counts[["Inactive"]] else 0
cat("Inactive values in current Bioassays matrix:", inactive_count, "\n")
## Inactive values in current Bioassays matrix: 0
# Missingness proxy: Not Measured rate per assay
not_measured_rate <- rowMeans(is.na(assay_mat_chr))
summary(not_measured_rate)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   0.867   0.946   0.988   0.959   0.989   1.000
bio_long <- as.data.frame(assay_mat_chr) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("assay") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-assay, names_to = "compound", values_to = "status")
bio_long$status <- factor(
  tidyr::replace_na(as.character(bio_long$status), "Not Measured"),
  levels = c("Active", "Inactive", "Not Measured")
)

ggplot(bio_long, aes(x = status)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  labs(
    title = "Bioassays overall category counts",
    x = "Outcome",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(bio_long, aes(x = assay, fill = status)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Bioassays outcome composition by assay",
    x = "Assay (AID)",
    y = "Fraction",
    fill = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

5.3 Tox21

A compound-by-assay matrix for the Tox21 panel. Rows are Tox21 assays and columns are PubChem CIDs. Values are typically binary (0/1) with missing values for unmeasured compounds.

se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[["Tox21"]]
assay_mat <- assay(se)

c(rows = nrow(assay_mat), cols = ncol(assay_mat))
## rows cols 
##   12 5396
assay_mat[1:min(5, nrow(assay_mat)), 1:min(6, ncol(assay_mat))]
# Value distribution
assay_mat_num <- as.matrix(assay_mat)
if ("mol_id" %in% rownames(assay_mat_num)) {
  assay_mat_num <- assay_mat_num[rownames(assay_mat_num) != "mol_id", , drop = FALSE]
}
table(as.vector(assay_mat_num), useNA = "ifany")
## 
##     0     1  <NA> 
## 49561  4233 10958
# Missingness per assay
summary(rowMeans(is.na(assay_mat_num)))
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##  0.0739  0.1302  0.1645  0.1692  0.2174  0.2624
tox21_long <- as.data.frame(assay_mat_num) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("assay") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-assay, names_to = "compound", values_to = "value")
tox21_long$value_factor <- factor(tox21_long$value, levels = c(0, 1))

tox21_compound_summary <- tox21_long |>
  group_by(compound) |>
  summarize(positive_count = sum(value == 1, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(compound_labels, by = c("compound" = "sample_id")) |>
  arrange(positive_count, compound)

tox21_plot_compounds <- bind_rows(
  tox21_compound_summary |> slice_head(n = 20) |> mutate(group = "Bottom 20"),
  tox21_compound_summary |> slice_tail(n = 20) |> mutate(group = "Top 20")
) |>
  distinct(compound, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(positive_count, compound)

tox21_plot <- tox21_long |>
  filter(compound %in% tox21_plot_compounds$compound) |>
  left_join(
    tox21_plot_compounds |>
      select(compound, compound_label),
    by = "compound"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    compound_label = factor(
      compound_label,
      levels = tox21_plot_compounds$compound_label
    )
  )

ggplot(tox21_plot, aes(x = compound_label, y = assay, fill = value_factor)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("0" = "#d1d5db", "1" = "#2563eb"), na.value = "#f3f4f6") +
  labs(
    title = "Tox21 outcomes (0/1) for compounds with the lowest and highest positive counts",
    x = "Drug name",
    y = "Assay",
    fill = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))

tox21_rate <- tox21_long |>
  group_by(assay) |>
  summarize(positive_rate = mean(value == 1, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(tox21_rate, aes(x = reorder(assay, positive_rate), y = positive_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Tox21 positive rate by assay",
    x = "Assay",
    y = "Positive rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

5.4 ToxCast

A compound-by-assay matrix for the ToxCast panel. Rows are assay endpoints and columns are PubChem CIDs. Values are typically binary (0/1) with missing values.

se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[["ToxCast"]]
assay_mat <- assays(se)[[1]]

c(rows = nrow(assay_mat), cols = ncol(assay_mat))
## rows cols 
##  617 6054
assay_mat[1:min(5, nrow(assay_mat)), 1:min(6, ncol(assay_mat))]
# Value distribution
assay_mat_num <- as.matrix(assay_mat)
table(as.vector(assay_mat_num), useNA = "ifany")
## 
##       0       1    <NA> 
## 1010677   93752 2630889
# Missingness per assay
summary(rowMeans(is.na(assay_mat_num)))
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   0.069   0.597   0.821   0.704   0.960   0.994
toxcast_counts <- as.data.frame(table(value = as.vector(assay_mat_num), useNA = "ifany"))

ggplot(toxcast_counts, aes(x = value, y = Freq)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  labs(
    title = "ToxCast value counts",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

row_non_missing <- rowSums(!is.na(assay_mat_num))
row_positive <- rowSums(assay_mat_num == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
row_rate <- row_positive / row_non_missing
row_rate <- row_rate[!is.na(row_rate)]

ggplot(tibble::tibble(positive_rate = row_rate), aes(x = positive_rate)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#3A6EA5", alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "ToxCast positive rate by assay",
    x = "Positive rate",
    y = "Assay count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

col_non_missing <- colSums(!is.na(assay_mat_num))
col_positive <- colSums(assay_mat_num == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
col_rate <- col_positive / col_non_missing
toxcast_compound <- tibble::tibble(
  compound = colnames(assay_mat_num),
  positive_rate = as.numeric(col_rate)
) |>
  left_join(compound_labels, by = c("compound" = "sample_id")) |>
  arrange(positive_rate, compound)

toxcast_top_compounds <- toxcast_compound |>
  slice_tail(n = 20) |>
  arrange(positive_rate, compound) |>
  mutate(
    display_label = ifelse(
      nchar(compound_label) > 40,
      paste0(substr(compound_label, 1, 37), "..."),
      compound_label
    ),
    display_label = factor(
      make.unique(display_label),
      levels = make.unique(display_label)
    )
  )

ggplot(
  toxcast_top_compounds,
  aes(x = display_label, y = positive_rate)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  labs(
    title = "ToxCast positive rate by compound (top 20)",
    x = "Drug name",
    y = "Positive rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, vjust = 1))

5.5 ClinTox

A compound-by-label matrix for clinical toxicity outcomes. Rows correspond to the ClinTox labels (e.g., FDA approval and toxicity) and columns are PubChem CIDs. Values are binary (0/1) with missing values for compounds not present in the source dataset.

se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[["ClinTox"]]
assay_mat <- assay(se)

c(rows = nrow(assay_mat), cols = ncol(assay_mat))
## rows cols 
##    2  885
assay_mat[1:min(5, nrow(assay_mat)), 1:min(6, ncol(assay_mat))]
# Value distribution
assay_mat_num <- as.matrix(assay_mat)
table(as.vector(assay_mat_num), useNA = "ifany")
## 
##   0   1 
## 867 903
# Missingness per label
summary(rowMeans(is.na(assay_mat_num)))
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##       0       0       0       0       0       0
clintox_counts <- as.data.frame(table(value = as.vector(assay_mat_num), useNA = "ifany"))

ggplot(clintox_counts, aes(x = value, y = Freq)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  labs(
    title = "ClinTox value counts",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

row_non_missing <- rowSums(!is.na(assay_mat_num))
row_positive <- rowSums(assay_mat_num == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
row_rate <- row_positive / row_non_missing

clintox_label <- tibble::tibble(
  label = rownames(assay_mat_num),
  positive_rate = as.numeric(row_rate)

ggplot(clintox_label, aes(x = reorder(label, positive_rate), y = positive_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#72B7B2") +

  ) +
  theme_minimal()

5.7 Fingerprints (Morgan count fingerprints)

Count-based Morgan fingerprints generated from SMILES for each compound using RDKit. Each fingerprint experiment is stored as a sparse matrix of feature counts with rows as fingerprint bins and columns as PubChem CIDs.

fp_names <- grep("^fingerprint\\.", experiment_names, value = TRUE)
fp_names
## [1] "fingerprint.Morgan.2.1024" "fingerprint.Morgan.2.2048"
## [3] "fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024" "fingerprint.Morgan.3.2048"
preferred_fp_names <- c(
  "fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024",
  "fingerprint.Morgan.3.2048",
  "fingerprint.Morgan.2.1024",
  "fingerprint.Morgan.2.2048"
)
selected_fp_name <- preferred_fp_names[preferred_fp_names %in% fp_names][1]
selected_fp_name
## [1] "fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024"
for (fp_name in fp_names) {
  se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[[fp_name]]
  assay_mat <- assays(se)[[1]]

  cat("\nFingerprint:", fp_name, "\n")
  cat("Dimensions:", nrow(assay_mat), "x", ncol(assay_mat), "\n")

  # Sparsity for sparse matrices
  if (inherits(assay_mat, "sparseMatrix")) {
    sparsity <- 1 - Matrix::nnzero(assay_mat) / length(assay_mat)
    cat("Sparsity:", round(sparsity, 4), "\n")
  }

  print(assay_mat[1:min(5, nrow(assay_mat)), 1:min(6, ncol(assay_mat))])
}
##

## Dimensions: 1024 x 422030 
## Sparsity: 0.956 
## 5 x 6 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
##    501 527 535 546 547 554
## V1   .   .   .   .   .   .

## Sparsity: 0.978 
## 5 x 6 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
##    501 527 535 546 547 554
## V1   .   .   .   .   .   .

## V3   .   .   .   .   .   .
## V4   .   .   .   .   .   .
## V5   .   .   .   .   .   .
## 
## Fingerprint: fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024 
## Dimensions: 1024 x 422030 
## Sparsity: 0.941 
## 5 x 6 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
##    501 527 535 546 547 554
## V1   .   .   .   .   .   .
## V2   1   .   .   .   .   .
## V3   .   .   .   .   .   .
## V4   .   .   .   .   .   .
## V5   .   .   .   .   .   1
## 
## Fingerprint: fingerprint.Morgan.3.2048 
## Dimensions: 2048 x 422030 
## Sparsity: 0.97 
## 5 x 6 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
##    501 527 535 546 547 554
## V1   .   .   .   .   .   .
## V2   1   .   .   .   .   .
## V3   .   .   .   .   .   .
## V4   .   .   .   .   .   .
## V5   .   .   .   .   .   .
for (fp_name in fp_names) {
  se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[[fp_name]]
  assay_mat <- assays(se)[[1]]

  col_nnz <- Matrix::colSums(assay_mat > 0)
  row_nnz <- Matrix::rowSums(assay_mat > 0)

  nnz_df <- tibble::tibble(
    count = c(as.numeric(col_nnz), as.numeric(row_nnz)),
    axis = rep(c("Compound", "Feature"), c(length(col_nnz), length(row_nnz)))
  )

  p_nnz <- ggplot(nnz_df, aes(x = count, fill = axis)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Fingerprint non-zero counts:", fp_name),
      x = "Non-zero features per entity",
      y = "Count",
      fill = ""
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

  nonzero_vals <- assay_mat@x
  val_df <- as.data.frame(table(value = nonzero_vals))

  p_vals <- ggplot(val_df, aes(x = value, y = Freq)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#3A6EA5") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Fingerprint count values:", fp_name),
      x = "Count value",
      y = "Frequency"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

  print(p_nnz)
  print(p_vals)
}

5.8 Computing with Morgan Fingerprints

We now turn to a machine learning task. We will be trying to predict the drugs mechanism of action (MOA) from the drug structures as stored in the fingerprints. Specifically we will try to classify drugs by how likely they are to cause liver injury based on their Drug Induced Liver Injury (DILI) severity score. First lets look at the counts of the scores:

col.Data <- colData(hdd_mae) |> as.data.frame()
table(col.Data$DILI.Severity)
## 
##      0      2      3      4      5      6      7      8 
## 421660     27    138     20     30      3     23     75

We will frame predicting DILI severity as a binary classification problem. To this we will subset the data into high DILI scores (scores of 7 or 8) and low DILI (scores of 2 or 3).

high.scores <- c(7,8)
low.scores <- c(2,3)

dili.High <- col.Data |> filter(DILI.Severity %in% high.scores) |> select(Pubchem.CID)
dili.Low <- col.Data |> filter(DILI.Severity %in% low.scores) |> select(Pubchem.CID)

Now lets make training and testing datasts using the first preferred Morgan fingerprint available in the MAE. The training set will be 80% of the data we have.

set.seed(1234)

if (is.na(selected_fp_name)) {
  stop("No Morgan fingerprint experiments are available in the HDD MAE.")
}

fps <- assay(experiments(hdd_mae)[[selected_fp_name]])
cat("Using fingerprint experiment:", selected_fp_name, "\n")
## Using fingerprint experiment: fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024
fp.cids <- colnames(fps)
high.cids <- intersect(as.character(dili.High$Pubchem.CID), fp.cids)
low.cids <- intersect(as.character(dili.Low$Pubchem.CID), fp.cids)

high.fps <- as.matrix(t(fps[, high.cids, drop = FALSE]))
low.fps <- as.matrix(t(fps[, low.cids, drop = FALSE]))

X <- rbind(high.fps, low.fps)
rownames(X)<-NULL
y <- c( rep(1,dim(high.fps)[1]), rep(0,dim(low.fps)[1]))

split.idx <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), dim(X)[1], replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.8, 0.2))

X.train <- X[split.idx,]
y.train <- y[split.idx]

X.test <- X[!split.idx,]
y.test <- y[!split.idx]

Lastly we fit a logistic regression model and evaluate our prediction in terms of classification accuracy:

model <- cv.glmnet(X.train, y.train, family = 'binomial')
preds <- as.numeric(predict(model,X.test,type='class'))

accuracy <- sum(y.test ==preds)/length(y.test)
accuracy
## [1] 0.688
